WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: The catalogue of the five bundled examples, in one place for the two things that read it: the landing page's example chips (web/src/routes/+page.svelte, which links each to /report/gallery/<id>/ and puts `description` in the chip's title) and the build-time prebake (web/scripts/prebake-gallery.mjs, which runs every analysis on each and writes static/gallery/<id>.json). `description` is the one-line 'Description & Biological Domain' cell of the HyphAeon README's 'Included Benchmark Datasets' table (veg/HyphAeon@phase-2a README.md), verbatim; `paper.taxa`/`paper.codons` are that table's N and L before duplicate pruning and the taxon cap; `reference_runtime_sec` is PLAN.md section 1's measured `hyphaeon meme` wall time on a laptop CPU, the fallback when the engine's fixtures/manifest.json `e2e_wall_seconds` is absent. RHO is NEXUS with its tree embedded, so it has no tree file. Order is the landing page's chip order: the two small ones first, then the two whose trees carry no branch lengths (so they run tree-free on TN93 distances, D22), then the largest. `dated` is a SECOND catalogue, for /time: the three examples that carry sampling dates. They are not prebaked and have no gallery record — /time runs the date review in the page from the file itself, so an entry needs only the file names and what a reader should expect to see. They were added because /time shipped with nothing to click: the dated examples lived in the engine checkout, so the one route whose whole subject is metadata had no data. Each carries its dates a different way, which is the point — the review stage is what this route exists to show, and one example per rule is what exercises it. `date_rule` names the rule the ingest should match and is a claim the page's own test asserts, not a label.

dated.name: H5N1 HA
dated.description: Avian influenza H5N1 haemagglutinin, Chinese provinces 1996-2005. The cheapest honest temporal run: every sequence is dated, the gate is clear, and the null is seconds.
dated.expect: 98 of 98 dated from the four-digit year at the end of each name.

dated.name: HIV-1 env gp160
dated.description: Korber's HIV-1 group M envelope panel, the dating flagship: its root-to-tip fit is the published estimate of the pandemic's common ancestor.
dated.expect: 142 of 143 dated from the two-digit isolate year; CONSENSUS carries none, so the undated-sequence gate asks before it drops it.

dated.name: H1N1 2009
dated.description: The 2009 pandemic's first eight months, dated to the day. The temporal pillar's acceptance example, and the slowest: 4,384 codons is about 20 s of model pass.
dated.expect: 95 of 100 dated from the decimal year in the pipe-delimited header; the five without one are undated.
